text:
Mike: Quick sync — thinking about a unified iterate() surface that works across Python/TS/Go for paginated + streaming model endpoints. Goals: simple resume, clear retry semantics, minimal transport leakage.
Anya: +1. Main tradeoff: expose resume token vs opaque iterator. If we expose token, apps can checkpoint, but surface becomes heavier.
Cheng: Transport-level retries are simpler but hide idempotency. For streaming tokens we need idempotent continuation or server-issued resume ids.
Sam: Proposal: default client-level retry for transient network errors; streaming read errors -> surface yields an error object with retry_hint; consumer chooses resume or fail.
Mike: example python ergonomic idea:
```py
for chunk in client.iter_completion(request):
    handle(chunk)
# maybe provide checkpoint = iterator.checkpoint()
```
Lia: TS shape:
```ts
for await (const page of client.paginate(req)) {
  // page.items
}
```
Anya: Go: explicit iterator.Next(ctx) + Iterator.ResumeToken() — keeps control.
Cheng: Backoff defaults: jittered exponential, max 1s for interactive, 5s for long polling. Keep config per-route.
Sam: Important: don't auto-retry semantic errors (400/403). Only idempotent safe HTTP methods or explicit resume tokens.
Mike: Question: where to put retry hooks/telemetry? SDK core should emit events; app can register callback to map to retries vs resumptions.
Lia: Also think about partial result semantics — when resuming, do we dedupe? Probably server-side sequence numbers are best.
Anya: Action items: draft small RFC with API sketches in Python/TS/Go + a matrix mapping retry types to code paths. I'll start a doc and ping reviewers.
Dev-Bot: Created doc draft at https://go/redwood/doc/iter-retry-surface-draft (private) :tada:
Cheng: ack. I'll add invariants around resume tokens and idempotency.
Mike: cool — we'll review Wed sync. :thumbsup:
